_meta.author: Eduventure (original questions)
_meta.note: Language Kingdom questions: English for primary, lower and upper secondary (15 each) and beginner Bahasa Melayu (15). In review until approved in /admin; the Malay questions need a native-speaker check. Contains answers: never imported by src/.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which greeting do we use in the morning?
questions.explanation: We say "Good morning" before 12 noon.
questions.objective: Use greetings for different times of day.
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.b: Good night is said before going to sleep.
wrong.c: Goodbye is said when leaving.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: One cat, two ___.
questions.explanation: Most nouns add -s for more than one: cats.
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.a: More than one needs the plural form.
wrong.b: We just add -s: cat → cats.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: I eat ___ apple every day.
questions.explanation: "Apple" starts with a vowel sound, so we use "an".
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.c: Before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u) we use "an".
wrong.a: "An" is used because we mean any one apple, said for the first time.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The opposite of "hot" is ___.
questions.explanation: Hot and cold are opposites.
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: True or false: the plural of "child" is "childs".
questions.explanation: Child is irregular: the plural is "children".
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.true: "Childs" is not a word; the plural of child is children.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: She ___ my sister.
questions.explanation: With he, she and it we use "is".
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.c: "Am" goes only with "I".
wrong.a: "Are" goes with you, we and they.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The cat is sleeping ___ the table. 🐱⬇️
questions.explanation: Under means below something.
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.b: On means on top of; the cat is below.
wrong.c: In means inside something.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Seven plus three is ___. (Write the number as a word.)
questions.explanation: 7 + 3 = 10, which we write as "ten".
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Put the words in order to say what you like to eat.
questions.explanation: English sentences usually go: who (I) – action (like) – what (nasi lemak).
questions.objective: Order words in a simple sentence.
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: ___ is your name?
questions.explanation: "What is your name?" asks for a name.
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.b: Where asks about places.
wrong.c: When asks about time.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: True or false: a sentence starts with a capital letter.
questions.explanation: Every sentence starts with a capital letter, like "My name is Aina."
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.false: Sentences always start with a capital letter.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The sky on a sunny day is ___.
questions.explanation: A clear daytime sky is blue.
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.c: Grass is green; a clear sky is blue.
wrong.a: The sky is dark only at night.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: My mother's mother is my ___.
questions.explanation: Your mother's mother is your grandmother (nenek).
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.b: An aunt is your mother's or father's sister.
wrong.c: A sister has the same parents as you.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The day after Monday is ___.
questions.explanation: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday…
questions.objective: Know the days of the week.
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: He ___ to school every day.
questions.explanation: In the simple present, he/she/it adds -s: he walks.
questions.objective: Use the simple present with he and she.
questions.alignment: Primary English (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris Tahun 3-6, CEFR A1).

wrong.c: With he, she and it the verb adds -s.
wrong.a: "Walking" needs "is" before it.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Yesterday I ___ to Penang.
questions.explanation: "Go" is irregular: the past is "went".
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.b: "Yesterday" means the past, so we need the past form.
wrong.c: "Goes" is present, for he/she/it.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Kuala Lumpur is ___ than Ipoh.
questions.explanation: Short adjectives add -er (doubling the last letter): big → bigger.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.a: Comparing two things needs the comparative form.
wrong.b: "Biggest" compares three or more.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: She ___ (buy) a new bag last week.
questions.explanation: "Buy" is irregular: buy → bought.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Look! The children ___ in the rain.
questions.explanation: For actions happening now: am/is/are + -ing.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.b: "Look!" shows it is happening now, so we use the present continuous.
wrong.c: It is happening now, not in the past.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: True or false: "information" can be made plural as "informations".
questions.explanation: "Information" is uncountable: we say "some information" or "a piece of information".
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.true: Uncountable nouns have no plural form.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: My birthday is ___ June.
questions.explanation: We use "in" with months and years.
questions.objective: Use in, on and at for time.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.c: "On" goes with days and dates.
wrong.a: "At" goes with clock times.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to "enormous".
questions.explanation: Enormous means very big, like huge.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.b: Tiny is the opposite.
wrong.c: Quick is about speed, not size.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Put the words in order to make a question.
questions.explanation: Questions often go: question word – do/does – subject – verb.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: I was tired, ___ I went to bed early.
questions.explanation: "So" introduces a result.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.c: "But" shows a contrast, not a result.
wrong.a: "Because" gives a reason; here we need the result.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Mount Kinabalu is the ___ (high) mountain in Malaysia.
questions.explanation: With "the" and three or more things, we use the superlative: highest.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: You ___ wear a helmet when you ride a motorcycle. It is the law.
questions.explanation: "Must" expresses a strong rule or obligation.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.a: "Might" is only a possibility, not a rule.
wrong.b: "Can" is about ability or permission, not a rule.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: True or false: the correct spelling is "beautiful".
questions.explanation: Beautiful: b-e-a-u-t-i-f-u-l.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: This book is ___. Give it to me!
questions.explanation: Possessive pronouns stand alone: mine, yours, his, hers.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.b: "My" needs a noun after it (my book).
wrong.c: "Me" is an object, not a possessive.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Please ___ your shoes before you enter the house.
questions.explanation: Take off = remove clothing. In many Malaysian homes we take off our shoes.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

wrong.a: Put on is the opposite: wearing them.
wrong.b: Look after means to take care of.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: One knife, two ___.
questions.explanation: Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knife → knives.
questions.alignment: Lower-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 1-3, CEFR A2-B1).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: I ___ never ___ snow.
questions.explanation: Life experience: have + past participle: I have never seen snow.
questions.objective: Use the present perfect for experiences.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

wrong.b: "Never" with life experience uses the present perfect.
wrong.c: Experiences are not described with the continuous.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Change to passive: "The students cleaned the classroom."
questions.explanation: Passive: object becomes subject + was/were + past participle (+ by …).
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

options.text: The classroom is cleaning by the students.
The classroom was cleaned by the students.

wrong.a: That changes the meaning completely.
wrong.b: The tense must stay past, and passive uses be + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the picnic.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present, will + verb.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

wrong.c: "Would" is for unlikely or imaginary situations (second conditional).
wrong.a: The result of a real future condition uses "will".

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: She said, "I am hungry." → She said that she ___ hungry.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the tense moves back: am → was.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: True or false: "Neither of the boys are ready." is correct.
questions.explanation: "Neither" is singular: "Neither of the boys is ready."
questions.objective: Make verbs agree with tricky subjects.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

wrong.true: "Neither" takes a singular verb, so it should be "is".

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The flood forced many families to ___ their homes.
questions.explanation: Evacuate means to leave a dangerous place.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

wrong.c: Evaluate means to judge something; it only looks similar.
wrong.a: Evaporate means to turn into vapour.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The teacher ___ taught us English has retired.
questions.explanation: We use "who" for people.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

wrong.b: "Which" is for things, not people.
wrong.c: "Whose" shows possession.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Put the sentences in order to make a short paragraph.
questions.explanation: Sequence words (first, next, finally) show the order.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

options.text: Next, cook it with coconut milk.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which is best for a formal letter?
questions.explanation: Formal letters use full words and polite, neutral language.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

options.text: I am writing to complain about the service.
Hey, the service was really bad lah.

wrong.c: "Hey" and "lah" are too informal for a formal letter.
wrong.a: Text spellings and strong slang are not used in formal writing.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: He spoke with great ___ (confident).
questions.explanation: After "great" we need a noun: confident → confidence.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: "It's a piece of cake" means…
questions.explanation: "A piece of cake" means something is very easy.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

wrong.a: It is an idiom, not about real cake.
wrong.b: The idiom is about how easy something is.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: I enjoy ___ novels in my free time.
questions.explanation: "Enjoy" + verb-ing: I enjoy reading.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

wrong.c: "Enjoy" is followed by the -ing form.
wrong.a: After "enjoy" we need a gerund.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: True or false: "Its raining" needs an apostrophe: "It's raining".
questions.explanation: "It's" = "it is", so it needs an apostrophe.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

wrong.false: "It's" is short for "it is" and needs the apostrophe.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: ___ the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
questions.explanation: "Despite" shows contrast: something happened even though…
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

wrong.a: Because of gives a cause; here the traffic did not stop us.
wrong.b: "So" introduces a result and cannot start this way.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: When we reached the station, the train ___ already ___ (leave). Write both words, e.g. "has gone".
questions.explanation: An earlier past action uses the past perfect: had + past participle.
questions.alignment: Upper-secondary English (e.g. KSSM English Form 4-5 / SPM, CEFR B1-B2).

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: How do you say "Good morning" in Malay?
questions.explanation: Selamat pagi = Good morning.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.b: Selamat malam = Good night.
wrong.c: Selamat tinggal = Goodbye, said by the person who is leaving (the one staying says "Selamat jalan").

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: What does "Terima kasih" mean?
questions.explanation: Terima kasih = Thank you.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.a: Excuse me = Maaf / Tumpang lalu.
wrong.b: You are welcome = Sama-sama.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: Which number is "lima"?
questions.explanation: Lima = five.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.c: 4 is empat.
wrong.a: 6 is enam.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: Satu, dua, ___, empat. (Write the missing number in Malay.)
questions.explanation: Satu (1), dua (2), tiga (3), empat (4).
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: What does "ibu" mean?
questions.explanation: Ibu = mother.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.a: Father = bapa or ayah.
wrong.b: Sister = kakak (older) or adik (younger).

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: True or false: "nasi" means rice.
questions.explanation: Nasi = cooked rice, as in nasi lemak.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: You are hungry. Which sentence fits?
questions.explanation: Lapar = hungry. Saya lapar = I am hungry.
questions.objective: Say how you feel in Malay.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.b: Haus means thirsty.
wrong.c: Penat means tired.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: Put the words in order: "My name is Adam."
questions.explanation: Malay says "Nama saya Adam" (name – my – Adam).
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: At the market you ask "How much is this?". You say…
questions.explanation: Berapa = how much; harga = price; ini = this.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.c: Apa khabar = How are you?
wrong.a: Di mana tandas = Where is the toilet?

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: The Malay word for "red" is ___.
questions.explanation: Merah = red, as in the Malaysian flag colours.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: What does "esok" mean?
questions.explanation: Esok = tomorrow.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.a: Yesterday = semalam.
wrong.b: Today = hari ini.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: True or false: "kami" and "kita" both mean "we".
questions.explanation: Both mean "we": kita includes the listener; kami does not.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.false: Both mean we; kita includes the person you are talking to, kami does not.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: What does "kanan" mean?
questions.explanation: Kanan = right, kiri = left.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.b: Left = kiri.
wrong.c: Straight = terus.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: Which word means "to eat"?
questions.explanation: Makan = eat. "Jom makan!" = Let's eat!
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.

wrong.a: Minum = to drink.
wrong.b: Tidur = to sleep.

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: Complete: "Saya ___ ke sekolah." (I go to school.)
questions.explanation: Pergi = to go. Saya pergi ke sekolah = I go to school.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu for beginners (CEFR A1), for learners new to Malay.
